parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a magnetic field.

markscheme_points.text: a region where a force acts on
a current-carrying conductor or a moving charge or a magnetic material / magnetic pole

hints: Hint 1: Start by thinking what any field means in physics - a region of space where something would feel an effect even without touching.
Hint 2: Now think what kind of object feels a magnetic push - what has to be moving or what kind of material must it be?
parts.proper_answer: A region of space where a force acts on a current-carrying conductor or a moving charge or a magnetic material / magnetic pole.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What a Field Means**
Think of a field as an invisible zone of influence. If you place the right kind of test object in that zone, it feels a force without contact.

Step 2: **What Feels a Magnetic Force**
Electric fields push any charge, gravitational fields pull any mass. Magnetic fields are more selective. They only push moving charges, currents which are streams of moving charges, and magnetic materials or poles. Put those two ideas together for the full definition.

parts.label: (b)

markscheme_points.text: spacing between circles increases with distance from wire
arrows showing direction of field is clockwise

hints: Hint 1: Picture looking along the wire. The field has no start or end, so what closed shape must the lines make centred on the wire?
Hint 2: Think how the field strength changes as you move away from the wire, and what that means for how tightly the lines should be packed.
Hint 3: Grip the wire in your mind with right thumb into the page. Which way do your fingers curl for the field direction?
parts.proper_answer: Four concentric circles centred on P, spacing increasing with radius, with clockwise arrows.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Shape of the Lines**
Around a long straight wire the field lines form complete loops with the wire at the centre. So draw four circles centred on the cross at P, one inside the other.

Step 2: **Spacing Shows Strength**
Field strength falls off with distance from the wire, $B \propto 1/r$. Where the field is weaker the lines are further apart. So make the gaps between successive circles get larger as you go outwards.

Step 3: **Direction by Right-Hand Grip**
Point your right thumb in the current direction, into the page. Your curled fingers give the field sense. Viewed from above this is clockwise. Add arrowheads on each circle pointing clockwise.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the magnetic force per unit length exerted on wire Q by wire P.

markscheme_points.text: force per unit length = BI = 2.6 × 10⁻³ × 5.0 = 0.013 N m⁻¹

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the wire Q sitting in the field of P. Which three quantities control the magnetic force on a straight current in a field perpendicular to it?
Hint 2: You need force for each metre, so think how to remove length from the calculation and remember to convert $2.6\text{ mT}$ to tesla.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Law for Force on a Current**
A current $I$ of length $L$ perpendicular to flux density $B$ feels $$F = BIL$$ Here the $2.6\text{ mT}$ field at Q is perpendicular to Q.

Step 2: **Force Per Unit Length**
Divide by $L$ to get force per metre: $$\frac{F}{L} = BI$$ Convert: $2.6\text{ mT} = 2.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$. Then $$\frac{F}{L} = 2.6 \times 10^{-3} \times 5.0 = 0.013\text{ N m}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the direction of the force exerted on wire Q by wire P.
hints: Hint 1: Use Fleming's left hand for wire Q: current is out of the page and the field from P at Q points downward, so which way must the push point?
parts.proper_answer: To the right, away from wire P.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Apply Fleming's Left Hand**
At Q, the field due to P with current into the page is clockwise, so on the right-hand side of P it points down. For Q, $I$ is out of the page. With middle finger out and index finger down, your thumb points to the right. The force on Q is to the right, so the wires repel.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The flux density of the magnetic field at wire P due to the current in wire Q is $1.5\text{ mT}$.

Determine the magnitude of the current in wire P. Explain your reasoning.

markscheme_points.text: force (per unit length) has the same magnitude due to Newton's 3rd

hints: Hint 1: Think about the pair of forces between the two wires. If P pushes Q to the right, what does Newton's third law say about Q pushing P?
Hint 2: That means the $0.013\text{ N m}^{-1}$ value also applies at P. Use the new $B$ value there to work back to the unknown current in P.
parts.proper_answer: By Newton's 3rd law force on P has same magnitude $0.013\text{ N m}^{-1}$. So $0.013 = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times I$, $I = 8.7\text{ A}$ in wire P.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Equal and Opposite Forces**
The magnetic forces between the wires are an action-reaction pair. Even though the $B$ values at the two positions differ, the force per unit length on P due to Q must equal that on Q due to P, so $$\left(\frac{F}{L}\right)_P = 0.013\text{ N m}^{-1}$$

Step 2: **Find Current in P**
At P, $$\frac{F}{L} = B_Q I_P$$ where $B_Q = 1.5\text{ mT} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$. So $$0.013 = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times I_P$$ $$I_P = \frac{0.013}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} \approx 8.7\text{ A}$$
